step1_analysis.description: This circuit acts as a harmonic sampler or mixer, likely part of the real-time active load-pull (RT-ALP) control network. It uses NMOS source followers to buffer RF inputs and NMOS switches to sample the signals onto a common output node with a PMOS active load.

paper_reference.title: High Efficiency RF Power Amplifier Designed With Harmonic Real-Time Active Load-Pull

operating_frequency.description: RF carrier frequency for the sampler/mixer.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by NMOS fT in sky130. 0.5um length has fT ~ 10-20GHz, so 2GHz is well within range.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 0.5um devices can easily operate at the 2GHz RF frequency reported in the paper.

sky130_expected.calculation: Set by the testbench LO source.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the paper's baseband envelope frequency for active load-pull.

output_power.description: Power delivered to the load at the output node.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_pk2pk ~ 1V into 100k ohm load. P = V^2/(8R) = 1.25uW = -29 dBm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: This is a small-signal sub-block in sky130, not the main 30V p-HEMT PA, so output power is drastically lower.

efficiency.description: Power added efficiency (PAE) or DC-to-RF efficiency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: As a sampler/mixer, it operates in Class A/AB with low efficiency compared to a switched-mode PA.

gain.description: Voltage conversion gain from RF input to sampled output.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Passive sampling and source followers provide no voltage gain, unlike the main PA.

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard nominal VDD for sky130 1.8V devices.
Input swing limited by VDD and Vth. Max linear swing ~ 0.5V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the order of magnitude for 1.8V CMOS linear range.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure AC bandwidth, transient mixing/sampling performance, output power, and efficiency of the harmonic sampler sub-block.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Harmonic Sampler / Mixer
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

XM1 VDD LABEL_NET_0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VDD LABEL_NET_1 N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N2 N3 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N2 N3 N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 VDD LABEL_NET_2 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 VDD LABEL_NET_3 N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N2 N2 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 VDD N2 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

* DC and AC Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
* RF Input at 2GHz
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 sin(0.9 0.9 2G)
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 dc 0.9
VLABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 dc 0.9
VLABEL_NET_3 LABEL_NET_3 0 dc 0.9
* Baseband/LO Input at 200kHz
VN3 N3 0 dc 0.9 sin(0.9 0.9 200k)

* Load resistors to provide DC path and simulate next stage
R1 N1 0 100k
R2 N0 0 100k
R3 N2 0 100k

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point
op
print v(N1) v(N2) v(N0)
let dc_power_op = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print dc_power_op

* 2. AC Analysis (Bandwidth / Gain)
ac dec 10 1k 10G
let gain_db = vdb(N1)
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=(max_gain-3) fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis (Mixing / Sampling)
* 200kHz period is 5us. Run for 10us.
tran 10p 10u
meas tran v_out_max max v(N2)
meas tran v_out_min min v(N2)
meas tran v_out_pk2pk pp v(N2)

* Calculate Output Power and Efficiency
let out_power_w = (v_out_pk2pk * v_out_pk2pk) / 800000
print out_power_w

meas tran avg_current avg i(VVDD)
let dc_power_tran = -avg_current * 1.8
let efficiency = (out_power_w / dc_power_tran) * 100
print efficiency

quit
.endc
.end
